MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The ultrasonic cleaner feels useful alongside my hardware and repair supplies because it could clean small fasteners and greasy parts before reassembly.",
    "The wire ferrule assortment fits my interest in practical assembly supplies, while the cutting wheels and inspection camera connect to metalworking and inspection tasks already reflected in my purchases."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "The EMF, sound and radiation meters measure things I have no current reason to investigate; owning a caliper and thermometer does not mean every measuring instrument is useful to me.",
    "The anatomy model and fishing magnet serve activities outside my repair projects, and the printer bed requires a specific printer need that my history does not establish.",
    "Another borescope would duplicate a tool I already own, and the unclear radiation-detector title leaves me unsure what I would actually receive."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "The recommendations seem to treat an interest in workshop tools as an interest in almost any specialized technical device.",
    "They seem to assume that buying a durable tool makes another similar tool a natural next purchase, even without a replacement need."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My repeated purchases of screws, rivets, rivet nuts and bolts suggest ongoing fastening and assembly work; supplies that support those tasks feel more relevant than unrelated instruments.",
    "Compatibility affects whether I can use an item now: the recommended cutting wheels are 4.5 inches while my previous wheels were 5 inches, and I would need to check the crimping requirements for the ferrules.",
    "Useful additions to my existing equipment, such as cleaning parts during repairs, feel more timely than duplicating equipment I already have."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations partly recognize my repair and fabrication interests but stretch them too broadly into specialized equipment without enough attention to current tasks, existing tools and compatibility."
}
